newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif, approves debt reduction plan.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif, approves debt reduction plan.

text.p: Orange County, Calif., supervisors approved a far-reaching program on Tuesday that would reduce county debt levels to "build trust" on Wall Street in the wake of its bankruptcy.
The Board of Supervisors, meeting in Santa Ana, voted 5-to-0 in favor of the "Credit and Debt Management" plan, developed by officials in the county's executive office.
"We are getting our house in order and we are taking steps to ensure it stays in order," Thomas Sacco, the county's financial planning manager, said after the vote.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments.
The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.

Under the county's "Credit and Debt Management" plan, the county would set aside at least $15 million a year from its fund balances. Last year, the county set aside $26 million from its 1996-1997 fund balance.
By restructuring its 1995 Teeter bonds, county officials could free up a total of $15 million in reserves, and generate $5 million a year for three years in additional revenues.
The county could also save about $9 million by settling bankruptcy-related creditor claims.
With these funds, the county should be able to build up a $140 million fund by fiscal year 2001-2002 to retire or defease outstanding county bonds, county officials said.
The goal of the program would be to reduce county debt per capita to $482 from $572, they said.
The county's chief financial officer, Gary Burton, said the program would help to "build trust with Wall Street, Main Street and Sacramento."
By reducing county debt levels, the program could help the county attain single-A debt ratings, Burton added.
Christopher Varelas, the county's financial advisor, said the program could also make it easier for the county to sell bonds on Wall Street by lowering its borrowing costs.
"This plan will prove to the financial markets that Orange County has a long-term view and recognizes the importance of taking proactive action to reach solid financial health," Varelas said.
